erun helps to run and manage multiple tenants/environments.

Verbosity levels:
  (none) info: only erun status output; external tool output is suppressed
  -v     debug: stream external tool output with high verbosity (helm --debug, kubectl --v=4, docker --progress=plain)
  -vv    trace: debug output plus erun command-trace lines for every action and decision

Dry-run:
  --dry-run runs the same resolution flow but skips mutating operations and implies trace verbosity.

Timing:
  --time prints the elapsed runtime after the command finishes

Usage:
  erun [flags]
  erun [command]

Examples:
  erun deploy --dry-run
  erun -v deploy
  erun -vv init -y
  alias tenant-environment='eval "$(erun open tenant environment --no-shell)"'

Available Commands:
  api         Run ERun backend API over HTTP
  app         Launch the ERun desktop app
  cloud       Cloud provider utilities
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  context     Manage ERun cloud Kubernetes contexts
  contribute  Run contribute-mode workflows that target the ERun source repository
  delete      Delete a tenant environment and tear down its remote runtime
  deploy      Roll the project's charts out to an environment
  devops      DevOps utilities
  doctor      Diagnose and repair an environment's runtime and config
  exec        Repository execution utilities
  help        Help about any command
  idle        Show environment idle stop status
  init        Initialize configuration for the current project
  list        List configured tenants and environments
  mcp         Run ERun as an MCP server over HTTP
  open        Open a shell in the tenant environment
  release     Cut a release: stamp the version, tag it, and push the tag
  sshd        Remote SSH utilities
  upgrade     Redeploy opted-in environments to the latest version for their channel
  version     Print build information

Flags:
      --dry-run         Resolve and trace mutating actions without executing them.
  -h, --help            help for erun
      --output string   Result format: text (default, human stream) or json (structured result on stdout for orchestrators). (default "text")
      --time            Print the elapsed runtime after the command finishes.
  -v, --verbose count   Increase verbosity: -v streams external tool output, -vv adds erun command traces.

Use "erun [command] --help" for more information about a command.
